heading: Context ownership and cache permission
body: Call Behaviors.create(ConfigurationClass, { partition, signal, timeoutMs }) yourself. Assign the returned context to the behaviors field of each service. The partition (a separate area of data for one owner) is required. Base it on authenticated ownership. Never base it on caller input that was not validated. Use fixed public partitions only for data that is meant to be public. In Yon, create and dispose of the context inside the invocation. There is no global container, and no object is reused across requests. For a shared cache, the application must select an external adapter. By default, each operation has a 10-second deadline, and at most 64 operations run at the same time. You can set timeouts from 1 ms to 60 seconds. The authorize hook receives the operation, cache, type, method and selected keyArguments. The authorize hook is a function that Tachyon calls to ask for permission. It must return the literal value true for every cache access, including hits and eviction (removing entries). Put every argument that changes the result into the cache key. The limits are 4 KiB for keys and 1 MiB for values. The limits are also 24 hours for TTL and 10,000 entries for each policy. The storage adapter must enforce the given quota and replace entries atomically. Tachyon does not control the physical capacity of an external database. A failure never runs side effects again without telling you.
